info.album: I Get Around (Live On The Ed Sullivan Show, September 27, 1964)

podcast.body: This song became The Beach Boys' first number one hit, with recording commencing in April 1964. Brian Wilson began incorporating additional session musicians to augment the core band, expanding the instrumental palette. The basic track featured Carl Wilson (lead and rhythm guitar), Alan Jardine (bass), Dennis Wilson (drums), and Brian Wilson (keyboards), enhanced by two six-string bass players (Glenn Campbell, May Pullman), two saxophones, and percussion (Hal Blaine). Unusually, the primary chordal support was provided by a harpsichord, an instrument Brian would frequently use in subsequent years. The lyrics, penned by Mike Love but reflecting Brian Wilson's sentiments, hinted at a desire for change and new experiences ("I'm getting both driving up and down the same old strip, I've got to find a new place where the kids are hip"). It achieved Top 10 status in the UK and became a particular favorite within London's mod subculture. "I get around is a worthy classic, but the B side, don't worry baby, is there anything even better?"
